newsitem.title: USA: U.S. deploys troops for possible Zaire evacuation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. deploys troops for possible Zaire evacuation.

text.p: The United States is sending hundreds of troops to West Africa to prepare for a possible evacuation of Americans from Zaire, the Pentagon said on Friday.

"The Department of Defense has directed the U.S. European Command to deploy enabling forces, consisting of several hundred personnel, as part of contingency planning for a possible future evacuation from Zaire," the Pentagon said in a written statement.

The forces included command-and-support elements for a forward joint task force and would go to several locations in West African countries including Brazzaville, Republic of Congo, and Libreville, Republic of Gabon, the statement said.

The deployment was another step in planning for contingency measures to ensure the security of U.S. citizens in Zaire if an evacution should become necessary, the Pentagon said, adding that it did not mean the removal of Americans was imminent.
The troops were heading for West Africa primarily from the Southern European Task Force based in Vicenza, Italy with some support elements from U.S.-based units.
Defense Secretary William Cohen said on Friday U.S. officials were monitoring the rebellion in Zaire day-by-day, even hour-by-hour, to assess whether to evacuate U.S. citizens.
